questions.prompt: You won two buy-ins at $1/$2 tonight. Moving to $5/$10 for the next hand is…

choices.text: A mistake. One session is not a bankroll or a skill proof.
Required, because winners must move up

questions.explanation: Stake choice is a money decision, not a celebration.

questions.prompt: $1/$2 with a drop makes which play less profitable than the unraked chart?

choices.text: A thin call of a small bet, and a steal of a tiny pot.
Getting a set all-in when you are a big favorite in a large pot

questions.explanation: The drop takes the edge off small pots. Big favorite pots still clear a capped rake.

questions.prompt: A $2/$5 game that is tougher and uses a percent rake, compared with a soft $1/$2, should be chosen when…

choices.text: Your edge is real and the buy-in does not threaten rent or food.
You are stuck in the $1/$2 game

questions.explanation: Higher stakes are not a reward. They are a higher price for the same mistakes.

questions.prompt: This app’s hands do not currently subtract rake. When you practice a close call you should remember…

choices.text: A live room may take that edge away. Do not treat a break-even unraked call as a must-call live.
The app’s result is the casino’s result
Time rake is dealt as a community card

questions.explanation: Practice the decision. Adjust the price when the house takes a piece.
